h1: Vela Ul — AI & SaaS Features Section Design
tagline: Features section reference for an AI or SaaS product, captured at 1920x1418 with the layout, timings and palette specified in the brief.
summary: Features section reference for an AI or SaaS product — cubic-bezier(.22,1.36,1) easing, a masked headline reveal, glass panels and a stats row.
about: Read Vela Ul as a features section spec: the values were written down before the page was built. The colour scheme is #16120C underneath and #F7F5F2 for the type, and the page is set in Arial, Helvetica. It ships as one self-contained HTML file, so the whole features section can be lifted into a project without a design handoff. The brief spends its motion budget on 720ms transitions, cubic-bezier(.22,1.36,1) and a looping video bed. It is most useful when the AI & SaaS features section has to survive a copy change without a redesign.

layout.title: Links before the action
layout.body: A short run of links and a single action sit over the features section, held at a fixed 25px display size and 100vh sections so the bar never competes with the composition behind it. Below 410px the links collapse instead of wrapping onto a second line.

layout.title: One media element carries the mood
layout.body: The composition is built on top of the 1920x1418 clip rather than beside it, so the media never gets a panel or a border. A poster frame at 1920x1418 holds the composition when autoplay is unavailable, so the layout never collapses.

layout.title: Figures at display size
layout.body: The figures are set in Arial, Helvetica at a size closer to the headline than to the body copy. Labels sit under the figures at the smallest step in the brief, so the row reads as data rather than decoration. If a figure needs a paragraph, it is not a stat.

layout.title: Behaviour is defined per width
layout.body: Type is sized with a clamp between 14px and 20px rather than fixed steps, so the display line stays proportionate between breakpoints instead of jumping. Because the scale is clamped, the display line never jumps between breakpoints.

motion.title: Timings in milliseconds
motion.body: Transitions are specified at 720ms using cubic-bezier(.22,1.36,1), which is the timing the controls are held to. The values are short enough to read as feedback rather than as animation. Keep the durations when you re-skin the page.

motion.title: Ambient motion without a scroll library
motion.body: Ambient movement comes from the 4.7s 1920x1418 loop rather than from scroll effects, which keeps the page calm and the type readable. The clip is short enough to loop without a visible seam, which matters more than its resolution.

style.glass: Panels are translucent over #16120C, and the type on top stays at full contrast so the effect never costs readability.

editorial.title: Making the features section yours
editorial.body: Re-skinning the palette first is the usual mistake. It changes the mood without touching the composition, and a fixed 25px display size and 100vh sections still carry the layout; do the copy and media first and the palette last. Keep the media crop; it is doing as much work as the type.

editorial.title: What an AI or SaaS product gains here
editorial.body: You could rebuild this as a stack of separate cards and lose only the argument. The features section reads as one decision instead: navigation, the headline, the announcement badge, the stats row and the card grid in a single sequence. Vela Ul states the offer once and lets the composition repeat it rather than adding a second claim.

editorial.title: How the features section reflows
editorial.body: Compared with a mobile layout that hides sections, this one keeps them and changes their shape: the scale is fluid rather than stepped, the layout shifts at 410px and the section is held at 100vh. Width changes the measurements, not the reading path.
